It is also called '''Kan'i Nijūroku-kai''' (冠二十六階), and sometimes written as '''Kan'i Nijūroku-kai Sei''' (冠位二十六階制) with the addition of "Sei" (制) meaning "system." It was a revision of the previous {{ill|Ritsuryō Nineteen Rank System|ja|冠位十九階|qid=Q11395034}} and was later abolished with the implementation of the {{ill|Ritsuryō Forty-Eight Rank System|ja|冠位四十八階|qid=Q135579719}}.

== Notes on the System ==
On '''February 9, 664''' (3rd year of Emperor Tenji’s reign), '''Crown Prince Naka no Ōe''' (later '''Emperor Tenji''') issued an '''imperial edict (Senmyō)''' through his brother, '''Prince Ōama''' (later '''Emperor Tenmu''').<ref>『{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}』, Book 27, Emperor Tenji, 3rd Year, 2nd Month, 丁亥 (9th day) entry.</ref>
This edict, known as the '''Kōshi no Senmyō (甲子の宣命)''', included revisions not only to '''Rank titles''' but also to '''uji no kami (氏上)''', '''kabane (部曲, kabe)''', and '''iebe (家部)'''.
== Evolution and Abolition ==
The system lasted through the reigns of '''Emperor Tenji''' and '''Emperor Tenmu''', but during this time, there were partial modifications:
- Introduction of '''Inner Ranks (内位) and Outer Ranks (外位)'''.
- Establishment of '''Rank Titles for Princes (諸王の位)'''.
The system was abolished on '''January 21, 685''' (14th year of Emperor Tenmu) with the adoption of the '''{{ill|Ritsuryō Forty-Eight Rank System|ja|冠位四十八階|qid=Q135579719}}'''.
== Key Modifications ==
Compared to the previous '''{{ill|Ritsuryō Nineteen Rank System|ja|冠位十九階|qid=Q11395034}}''', the new system:
- Divided '''Hana (花), Yama (山), and Otsu (乙)''' into three levels ('''Upper, Middle, Lower''').
- Changed '''Hana (花)''' to '''Kin (錦)'''.
- Increased Ranks from 19 to '''26'''.
== Later Adjustments in the Tenji-Tenmu Transition ==
Historical records suggest further changes '''after 673''', especially:
- '''Outer Ranks (外位)''' were introduced to distinguish '''regional officials from capital officials'''.<ref>喜田新六「位階制の変遷について」</ref>
- '''Ranks for Royalty (諸王の位)''' were established.
